json.title: Simple Spring Boot API – requirements
json.summary: Requirements derived from the simple-springboot-api BRD (local demonstration application).

requirements.title: Welcome endpoint
requirements.statement: GET /api/hello must return HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing a welcome message.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/hello returns status 200
The body is JSON with a non-empty string field 'message'

requirements.title: Application information endpoint
requirements.statement: GET /api/info must return HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing the application name, version and description.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/info returns status 200
The body has string fields 'name', 'version' and 'description'

requirements.title: Products endpoint
requirements.statement: GET /api/products must return HTTP 200 with a JSON array of exactly three predefined products, each with id, name, description and price.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/products returns status 200
The body is a JSON array with exactly 3 elements
Each element has 'id', 'name', 'description' and 'price'

requirements.title: Technology baseline
requirements.statement: The application must be built with Maven and run on Java 21 with Spring Boot 3.x.
acceptance_criteria: `mvn verify` succeeds with JDK 21
The Spring Boot parent version is 3.x

requirements.title: Layered structure
requirements.statement: The code must separate controllers, services and models into distinct packages, with controllers delegating to services.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 3 endpoints is handled by a controller that calls a service
Models contain no web or service logic

requirements.title: Response time
requirements.statement: Each endpoint must respond within 500 ms at the 95th percentile on a local developer workstation.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency of each endpoint <= 500 ms over 100 local requests
requirements.rationale: The BRD only says 'promptly'; 500 ms p95 is a proposed, testable target (ISS-001).

requirements.title: Automated tests
requirements.statement: The build must run unit tests for the service logic and integration tests for all 3 endpoints that verify HTTP status 200 and the JSON structure.
acceptance_criteria: `mvn test` runs at least 1 service unit test and 3 endpoint integration tests
All tests pass

requirements.title: No security layer
requirements.statement: The application must not include authentication, authorization or Spring Security and is intended for local use only.
acceptance_criteria: The build has 0 dependencies on spring-boot-starter-security
No endpoint requires credentials

business_rules.statement: Product data consists of exactly three predefined products held in application memory and is not persisted across restarts.
No database, external API or external service may be introduced.

domain_concepts.name: Product
domain_concepts.definition: An item offered by the demonstration catalogue.

domain_concepts.name: Application information
domain_concepts.definition: Descriptive metadata of the running application.

domain_concepts.name: Welcome message
domain_concepts.definition: Greeting returned by the welcome endpoint.

issues.description: NFR-003 says responses must be returned 'promptly' without a measurable target.
issues.question: Is 500 ms at the 95th percentile on a developer workstation acceptable?

out_of_scope.reason: Executive summary; restated by the functional requirements
Business objectives; realised by REQ-F-001…003 and the EAEH lifecycle itself
Project risks; carried into the HLD risk register
Deliverables of the engineering process, not product requirements

json.title: Simple Spring Boot API – high-level design
json.summary: One Spring Boot application with layered packages and in-memory data, run locally.

context.description: Local REST API exposing welcome, application information and product endpoints.

actors.name: API client (developer)
actors.description: Calls the endpoints locally (curl, browser, tests)

components.name: Spring Boot API application
responsibilities: Hold the three products in memory

data_flows.data: HTTP GET requests and JSON responses

decisions.title: Single Spring Boot application with layered packages
decisions.context: The BRD asks for a simple layered architecture and no distributed architecture.
decisions.decision: Build one Spring Boot application with controller, service and model packages.

decisions.title: In-memory product data instead of a database
decisions.context: Products are static and no database may be introduced.
decisions.decision: A service holds an immutable list of the three predefined products.
consequences: Data resets on restart (accepted by the BRD)

decisions.title: No security layer
decisions.context: Authentication, authorization and Spring Security are explicitly out of scope; local use only.
decisions.decision: Do not add spring-boot-starter-security or any authentication.
consequences: Must never be deployed beyond a local workstation

decisions.title: Test approach with JUnit 5 and MockMvc
decisions.context: Unit tests for services and integration tests for every endpoint are required.
decisions.decision: Plain JUnit 5 tests for the service and Spring Boot tests with MockMvc for the three endpoints.

risks.mitigation: Verify JDK 21 before building (maven-enforcer or documented prerequisite)
Use the Spring Boot parent BOM and the Maven Wrapper
Keep to the three endpoints and the layered packages

tradeoffs.rationale: Meets the no-database constraint with the least complexity

json.title: Simple Spring Boot API – low-level design
json.summary: Packages, endpoints, models, sequences and local run configuration.

modules.name: controller
modules.responsibility: HelloController, InfoController, ProductController – map GET endpoints, return JSON

modules.name: service
modules.responsibility: InfoService (reads name/version/description from build info), ProductService (immutable list of 3 products)

apis.summary: JSON array of exactly 3 Product objects

decisions.title: Java records and constructor injection
decisions.context: Models are immutable and services are injected into controllers.
decisions.decision: Use Java records for models and constructor injection for services.

alternatives.option: Lombok data classes and field injection
